counterhypotheses.statement: Organism-level closed recurrence is required, but most current named organs/regulators may be compressible into a much smaller closed-loop state machine without losing the defining closure properties.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Keep action/world/outcome/credit/re-entry and persistent goal state fixed; progressively fuse/remove internal mechanisms while measuring causal signature, restart continuity, self-correction, long-horizon coherence and resource cost.

counterhypotheses.statement: Closure is necessary but deep recurrence is usually harmful; a shallow one-pass-or-one-retry controller may dominate most tasks.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Fixed-1 vs fixed-K vs adaptive recurrence with error-introduction, correction, stagnation, latency and OOD transfer.

counterhypotheses.statement: For within-pass reasoning, a model-native workspace can provide access/broadcast functions without architectural recurrence; ClayGWT adds value only at cross-organ/cross-cycle boundaries.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Native workspace intact/lesion/steer × ClayGWT truthful/shuffled/no-reentry split by automatic vs complex tasks.

counterhypotheses.statement: Explicit ClayGWT may be causally redundant once equivalent information is available through native/shared model state.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Information-equivalent lesion while preserving model/native access; compare receiver use, outcome, re-entry and long-horizon coherence.

counterhypotheses.statement: Epoch/provenance plus current/historical labels already capture practical temporal needs; full bitemporal semantics adds write/query complexity without enough benefit.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Temporal conflict suite with stale-fact errors, historical queries, write amplification, storage and latency.

counterhypotheses.statement: Branch DAGs preserve too much dead history and bias future cognition; linear checkpoints plus explicit alternatives are sufficient.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Matched rollback/recovery tasks measuring storage amplification, false branch revival, recovery latency and outcome.

counterhypotheses.statement: Most apparent higher-order dependencies are reducible to weighted pairwise interactions and should never become hyperedges/organ-emergence claims.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Fit pairwise projection then test residual interventional synergy/PEID and lesion-rescue incremental utility.

counterhypotheses.statement: Build, state, capability, GWT, reward and data consumption differ enough that one common provenance primitive becomes an unsafe abstraction; local guards are better.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Common fault matrix comparing typed shared vocabulary vs branch-local implementations on false reject, missed faults, recovery and complexity.

counterhypotheses.statement: Deterministic fold solves duplicate consumption but not current frontier completeness, delayed causal credit or sparse verified outcomes.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Concurrent terminal arrivals, ACK loss, rollback resurrection, delayed credit and source-lineage replacement.

counterhypotheses.statement: LCOP/model-latent measurement is too model/build-specific and costly to improve Frank beyond system receipts and observable loop dynamics.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Held-out predictive/control gain minus latency/VRAM/complexity, with binary transfer and intervention specificity.

counterhypotheses.statement: Different hardness levels inside one ClayCode runtime increase semantic boundary mistakes; uniform typed semantics may be simpler and safer.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Mutation/fuzz suite comparing selective vs uniform enforcement under code size, compile time, runtime overhead and false acceptance.

counterhypotheses.statement: Conjunctive ProductStart/Resume verification may accumulate redundant gates; a small set of cryptographic/state root attestations could logically imply multiple subchecks.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: Construct implication graph and adversarial substitutions; remove each gate only if no unique fault class escapes and recovery remains equivalent.

explicitly_rejected_counterframing.statement: A LangGraph/MAF-like durable workflow with memory and effect gates is architecturally equivalent to Frank's full recurrent organism if benchmark outputs match.
explicitly_rejected_counterframing.reason: It tests output equivalence while deleting the architecture property under study: persistent operational closure across internal state, world action, verified outcome, causal credit and re-entry. Such systems remain valid implementation/cost baselines for subfunctions only.
